items.title: AWS Ships Claude Apps Gateway as Self-Hosted Control Plane for Claude Code and Claude Desktop
items.summary_1line: AWS and Anthropic have released the Claude apps gateway for AWS, a self-hosted control plane that centralizes identity, policy, telemetry, routing, and spend caps for Claude Code and Claude Desktop. The gateway runs a...
items.editor_note: InfoQ's independent coverage confirms it shipped, detailing the identity, policy, telemetry, routing, and spend-cap features.

editorial.tldr: AWS and Anthropic introduced the Claude apps gateway on Jul 8, pitching it as a self-hosted control plane giving organizations a single point of control over access, cost, and policy for Claude Code and Claude Desktop.
editorial.whats_new: InfoQ's Jul 15 coverage confirms AWS shipped the gateway, centralizing identity, policy, telemetry, routing, and spend caps for Claude Code and Claude Desktop deployments.
editorial.why_it_matters: A self-hosted control plane gives platform teams centralized spend caps, policy, and telemetry for agentic coding tools instead of per-seat API keys — the governance layer most teams currently build in-house.
editorial.take_for_builders: If you're running Claude Code or Claude Desktop at scale on AWS, evaluate the apps gateway now — it centralizes identity, policy, telemetry, routing, and spend caps instead of per-seat API keys.

status.detail: Self-hosted control plane for Claude Code and Claude Desktop went from announcement to independently-confirmed shipping within a week.
